chung.Syllabus Name: Professional Project Management_Quản trị dự án
chung.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 140h online + 3h offline + 1h Final exam + 6 self-study
chung.Description: In this program, students are introduced to the foundations of project management through a hands-on, practice-based curriculum developed by Google experts. Over seven courses, students will explore both traditional and Agile approaches, gaining skills in risk management, budgeting, stakeholder communication, and team coordination. With more than 140 hours of interactive learning and real-world simulations, the program emphasizes practical application of project management tools and methods. Upon completion, students will be prepared for entry-level roles in project management and will be equipped with industry-recognized training that can lead to globally valued certifications and diverse career opportunities.
chung.StudentTasks:
1. Join the online course(s) when being invited by the admin.
2. Enroll in the courses, regularly study the course at least 5hrs/week by watching videos, reading materials, taking quizzes, doing assignments... as required
3. Respect the Coursera Code of Conduct, at https://learner.coursera.help/hc/en-us/articles/208280036-Coursera-Code-of-Conduct
4. Keep up with online learning progress (bonus will be awarded)
5. Communicate and discuss in forum
6. Attend offline sessions in the Campus (Optional)
7. Must complete the course(s) with certification(s) in order to take the Final Exam at Campus
chung.Note:
1) Ongoing assessment: Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded.
2) Theoretical Exam (TE)
3) Final Result (FR) = min (10, TE + Bonus)
4) Completion Criteria: TE>=4 and FR>=5

clo: Students will be able to describe and explain fundamental concepts and processes of project management in both traditional and Agile approaches.
Students will be able to apply project management tools and techniques (planning, risk management, budgeting, procurement) to design and implement a simulated project.
Students will be able to analyze and address project challenges, including change management, team conflicts, and stakeholder engagement, and propose appropriate solutions.

Students will be able to evaluate and design project management solutions using modern tools and methodologies (Agile/Scrum), and propose optimized approaches to improve project performance and success.
